newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council of Europe sends peace mission to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe sends peace mission to Albania.

text.p: The Council of Europe, voicing concern over the state of emergency in Albania, sent a mission to Tirana on Wednesday to try to help restore peace and dialogue between government and opposition.

The four-member delegation, headed by the vice-president of the 40-state body's parliamentary assembly Rene van der Linden of the Netherlands, was due in Tirana during the day. It planned to meet President Sali Berisha and seek contact with all political forces during its two-day visit.

The council's Secretary-General Daniel Tarchys, in a message to the Albanian government, offered "to assist towards the re-establishment of full respect for pluralist democracy, human rights and the rule of law".

Albania has been rocked by violent unrest that followed the collapse of high-risk pyramid investment funds. The government declared emergency rule and said it was determined to crush the unrest, which has claimed at least 20 lives.
Tarchys expressed concern that the state of emergency threatened human rights and freedom of movement and expression.
He reminded Tirana authorities that they were bound by the European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms, and had to inform the council of the measures they were taking.
Albania has been a party to the convention since October.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) has decided to send a fact-finding mission to Albania but said it might be delayed beyond this week's planned departure.

"I can only hope that the Albanian president will find the possibility of a political solution to this problem because what is going on and what could happen there is really tragic," he said.
French officials said the political solution would be likely to involve an electoral process.

At least 20 people have died in unrest in Albania following the collapse of high-risk investment funds. Under a state of emergency, army and police forces pushed towards the south on Wednesday to quash an armed rebellion and fighting was reported near the Adriatic town of Sarande.
